    spec multiaxis_control: Shared sin/cos unit for a 16-axis motor-control loop: a 1 MHz control tick issues 32 requests at once (Park + inverse Park per axis); all 32 results must be back within 0.44 us of the tick (p99 over ticks). Max error <= 2^-12. Minimise LUTs + FFs.
      constraint: throughput_msps >= 32
      constraint: max_abs_err <= 0.000244141
      constraint: sys_p99_batch_us <= 0.44
      objective: min luts_plus_ffs (HV ref 4000)
      objective: max accuracy_bits (HV ref 12)
      select: min luts_plus_ffs
      system (simulated at L2 for the shortlist; screened at L1 by an analytic bound): control loop: a tick every 1 us issues 32 requests at once (32 requests/us on average)
      budget: 400 evals, 100/round, <= 4 rounds, eps 0.01

args.notes: Spec: 32 requests per 1us tick, all results back within 0.44us p99, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs. Throughput >= 32 MSPS. Lessons: pipelined_m won the bursty spec (bursts of 8, p99 0.4us) with dw=15, n_iter=14, m=7 (855 LUTs+FFs, 59.6 MSPS, sim p99 0.233us). Here bursts are 4x larger (32) with the same 0.44us window, so a deeper pipeline (larger m) is likely needed to drain 32 requests in ~0.44us; pipelined_m family is the prime candidate. pipelined (m=1) reached fronts in high-rate specs. unrolled_k has never reached a front on this device - deprioritize. L1 analytic p99 bound was optimistic vs SimPy in the bursty spec, so keep margin on the p99 constraint.

args.lesson: For the 16-axis control spec (32 req/tick, p99 <= 0.44us, err <= 2^-12, min LUTs+FFs), pipelined_m dw=18, n_iter=16, no guards, round, m=4 won: 1236 LUTs+FFs est, 13 acc bits, 97.8 MSPS, simulated p99 0.378us. Key lesson: the m=5/dw=15 designs (1070-1145 LUTs) looked cheaper at L1 (analytic p99 0.434) but SimPy gave 0.4465 -> failed the 0.44us bound by 1.5%; L2 flipped the winner to the m=4/dw=18 design. The L1 analytic p99 bound is optimistic for bursty 32-request ticks; keep >= ~5% margin on the p99 constraint before trusting L1. No L3/L4 measured rows; back_annotate no_measured_data, finalize directly after L2.
